criteria.reasoning: The memo states 'We cannot move it, lend it, or apply this year's distribution to operations' and that the Board cannot 'Release or modify the purpose restriction at the October 21 meeting', concluding 'take no action on the Ruiz endowment.'

It identifies donor consent as a route: 'UPMIFA allows release or modification of a donor restriction only with the donor's consent under §6(a)', and 'the cleanest long-term route is written donor consent under UPMIFA §6(a)... That requires outreach to Ellen M. Ruiz.' It never says consent could not reach general operations.

The memo never addresses whether §6(d) is available for the Ruiz fund. It does not say §6(d) is unavailable or cite the fund's $512,860 value or 2017 establishment as reasons, as the PASS text requires.

It explains that court relief is §6(c) cy pres with notice to the Attorney General, quotes counsel that 'a budget shortfall at the institution does not, by itself, make a fund's purpose impracticable or impossible', and states 'Impracticability is not shown while ADN is active.'
It states we cannot 'Move corpus, accumulated earnings, or any portion of the FY2027 distribution into general operations' and that 'The 4% FY2027 distribution must go to ADN scholarships.'
It sums the twelve quarter-end values to '$5,930,200', averages them to '$494,183.33', and gives '4% = $19,767.33', which 'must be paid out as scholarships to ADN students.'
It says 'If the ADN program ever closes, gift agreement §5 already lets the Board redirect distributions ... That is not the situation today.' It does not rely on Section 5 now.
It rejects Joan's loan: 'This is precluded by Endowment Policy §4.2, on its face', quoting the bar on lending 'whatever the term or rate of the loan', and says 'I do not recommend pursuing it.'

It concludes §6(d) applies and lists all three reasons: 'Fund value under $25,000 — $18,420'; 'More than 20 years since established — 32 years'; and the purpose is impossible because 'the Secretarial Studies certificate is discontinued', closed June 30, 2011.

It schedules the AG notice 'On or before Monday, October 5, 2026' and says the '60-day §6(d) waiting period expires December 4, 2026 ... The Board cannot validly release the restriction before this date.' The October 21 meeting is limited to 'Authorizations only — no release yet.'

It states '§6(d) does not let the Board redeploy Calloway money to general operations', that the fund should go to 'an annual award for an Office Administration A.A.S. graduating student', and that this 'does not put money toward the FY2027 operating deficit.'

It identifies the 'Operating Reserve — $240,000 (board-designated, unrestricted)' as releasable 'by majority vote of the full Board. No donor consent; no Attorney General notice; no waiting period.' It recommends releasing $180,000 to close the gap.

All rules, thresholds, dates and values ($25,000, 20 years, 60 days, $512,860, $18,420, $240,000, the quarter-end values, counsel Larch & Pemberton, the October 5 letter) trace to the files or follow by arithmetic. No invented donor consent, alternative threshold or approval appears.
